questions.q:
Consider the following statements about computer graphics.
I. Raster graphics store a picture as mathematical descriptions of lines and curves.
II. Vector graphics become blocky when they are enlarged.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Vector graphics store geometric descriptions and scale without loss. Raster graphics store a grid of pixels and become blocky when enlarged.

questions.q: In a CRT display, electrons are emitted by the ______.
questions.e: The heated cathode in the electron gun emits the electron beam. The beam is focused and deflected, and strikes the phosphor coating to produce light.

questions.q: The number of times per second that the picture on a raster display is redrawn is called the ______.
questions.e: Refresh rate is the number of frames redrawn per second, commonly 60 Hz or more, to avoid flicker. Resolution counts pixels, not redraws.

questions.q: What is the size of the frame buffer needed for a display of 1024 × 768 pixels with 8 bits per pixel?
questions.e: Pixels = 1024 × 768 = 786432. At 1 byte per pixel this is 786432 bytes = 768 KB.

questions.q: The aspect ratio of a display whose resolution is 1920 × 1080 is ______.
questions.e: Divide both by 120: 1920/120 = 16 and 1080/120 = 9, so the ratio is 16:9.

questions.q: On a 0-255 scale, the CMY values of the RGB colour (255, 0, 0) are ______.
questions.e: C = 255 − R = 0, M = 255 − G = 255 and Y = 255 − B = 255. So pure red needs full magenta and yellow, with no cyan.

questions.q: Which of the following is true of Bresenham's line algorithm as compared with the DDA algorithm?
o: It uses floating-point multiplication at every step
It cannot draw lines with negative slope
It draws only horizontal and vertical lines
questions.e: Bresenham's algorithm uses an integer decision parameter with additions and shifts only. The DDA rounds floating-point increments at each step.

questions.q: A point (3, 4) is scaled about the origin with scaling factors sx = 2 and sy = 3. The new point is ______.
questions.e: Scaling multiplies each coordinate by its factor: x' = 3 × 2 = 6, y' = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a B-spline curve over a Bezier curve?
o: Local control of the curve shape
The curve always passes through all control points
The curve always has a higher degree
questions.e: In a B-spline, moving one control point alters only a part of the curve (local control), and the degree is independent of the number of control points. In a Bezier curve the degree is tied to the count.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Cohen-Sutherland line clipping.
I. The region code of a point inside the clipping window is 0000.
II. Each bit of the 4-bit region code shows whether the point lies beyond one edge (top, bottom, right or left) of the window.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. A point inside violates no edge, so all four bits are 0, and each bit marks one edge.

questions.q: What is the full form of JPEG?
questions.e: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that defined the lossy image compression standard.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the GIF image format.
I. A GIF image can have about 16.7 million colours in its palette.
II. GIF supports simple animation by storing several frames.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. GIF uses an 8-bit indexed palette of at most 256 colours. It does support simple animation.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a lossy compression format?
questions.e: FLAC is lossless compression, so the original audio can be restored exactly. MP3, JPEG and AAC discard some information.

questions.q: Animation on a screen works because of the ______ of the human eye.
questions.e: The eye retains an image for a fraction of a second, so rapidly displayed successive frames blend into smooth motion.

questions.q: A line is drawn from (2, 3) to (10, 8) using Bresenham's algorithm (slope less than 1, x sampled at unit steps). The initial decision parameter p₀ = 2Δy − Δx equals ______.
In the midpoint circle algorithm, the initial decision parameter for a circle of radius r = 10 centred at the origin is p₀ = 1 − r. Its value is ______.
questions.e: p₀ = 1 − r = 1 − 10 = −9. A negative value means the midpoint is inside the circle, so the next pixel is chosen at the same y.

questions.q: The point (3, 4) is rotated by 90° anticlockwise about the origin. The new coordinates are ______.
questions.e: x' = x cosθ − y sinθ = −4 and y' = x sinθ + y cosθ = 3 for θ = 90°. So the result is (−4, 3). (4, −3) is the clockwise rotation.

questions.q: The point (1, 2) is first scaled by 2 in both directions about the origin and then translated by (3, 1). The final position is ______.
questions.e: Scaling gives (2, 4). Translation then gives (5, 5). Doing the translation first gives (4, 3), then scaling gives (8, 6), so the order matters.

questions.q: A point (1, 3) is sheared along the x-direction with shear factor shx = 2, using x' = x + shx·y and y' = y. The result is ______.
questions.e: x' = 1 + 2 × 3 = 7, and y' stays 3. So the sheared point is (7, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bezier curves.
I. A cubic Bezier curve is determined by four control points.
II. A Bezier curve always passes through all of its control points.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: A Bezier curve of degree n uses n + 1 control points, so a cubic uses four. It passes through only the first and last control points, while the others pull the curve.

questions.q: The Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm is used for clipping ______.
o: a polygon against a convex clip window, one edge at a time
a line against a rectangle using region codes
a curve against a circular window
questions.e: Sutherland-Hodgman clips a polygon successively against each edge of the clip window, passing the output list of vertices to the next edge. Region codes belong to Cohen-Sutherland line clipping.

questions.q: A clipping window is 0 ≤ x ≤ 10 and 0 ≤ y ≤ 10. Using the bit order Top, Bottom, Right, Left, the region code of the point (12, −3) is ______.
questions.e: x = 12 is right of the window, so R = 1. y = −3 is below it, so B = 1. T and L are 0, giving 0110.

questions.q: Which of the following is an image-space hidden surface removal method?
questions.e: The Z-buffer algorithm compares depth at each pixel, so it works in image space. Back-face detection and depth sorting work on objects (object space).

questions.q: In Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG), complex solids are built from primitives such as cubes and cylinders using ______.
o: polygon meshes of faces and edges
Boolean operations: union, intersection and difference
questions.e: CSG combines solid primitives with union, intersection and difference, stored as a tree. The boundary representation (B-rep) uses faces, edges and vertices instead.

questions.q: Uncompressed video has a frame size of 640 × 480 pixels, 24 bits per pixel and 30 frames per second. The data rate is ______ bytes per second.
questions.e: One frame = 640 × 480 × 3 bytes = 921,600 bytes. At 30 frames per second this is 27,648,000 bytes per second.

questions.q: Bresenham's algorithm draws a line from (0, 0) to (5, 2) using p₀ = 2Δy − Δx, with p → p + 2Δy if p < 0, else y increases and p → p + 2(Δy − Δx). The pixels plotted are ______.
questions.e: p₀ = 2(2) − 5 = −1, so y stays 0 at x = 1 and p = 3. Then y = 1 at x = 2 (p = −3), y = 1 at x = 3 (p = 1), y = 2 at x = 4 (p = −5), and y = 2 at x = 5.

questions.q: The point (3, 1) is rotated by 90° anticlockwise about the point (1, 1) using homogeneous coordinates (translate, rotate, translate back). The new position is ______.
questions.e: Translate by (−1, −1): (2, 0). Rotate 90° anticlockwise: (0, 2). Translate back: (1, 3). (−1, 3) results if the rotation is done about the origin.

questions.q: A system has a 1280 × 1024 display. Each pixel stores an 8-bit index into a colour look-up table of 256 entries of 24 bits each. The total memory for the frame buffer plus the look-up table is ______ bytes.
questions.e: Frame buffer = 1280 × 1024 × 1 byte = 1,310,720 bytes. Table = 256 × 3 bytes = 768 bytes. Total = 1,311,488. Direct 24-bit storage would need 3,932,160.

questions.q: A window is 0 ≤ x ≤ 10, 0 ≤ y ≤ 10. A line from P₁(−4, 2) to P₂(6, 12) is clipped by Cohen-Sutherland. After clipping against the left edge x = 0, the new endpoint replacing P₁ is ______.
questions.e: The slope is (12 − 2)/(6 + 4) = 1. At x = 0, y = 2 + 1 × (0 + 4) = 6. The endpoint codes (0001 and 1000) have AND = 0000, so the line is neither trivially accepted nor rejected.

questions.q: A cubic Bezier curve has control points P₀(0,0), P₁(0,4), P₂(4,4) and P₃(4,0). The point on the curve at t = 0.5 is ______.
